surfaces.description: Concise markdown index of every page and machine-readable resource.

surfaces.description: Full plain-text export of all published content plus the scorecard snapshot.

surfaces.name: WebMCP tools
surfaces.description: Six tools registered on document.modelContext for in-browser agents, four read and two write. Callable only from a browser that implements WebMCP; the definitions are at https://www.mattpyle.com/webmcp/tools.json and the data they read is at https://www.mattpyle.com/webmcp/index.json.

surfaces.name: A2A Agent Card
surfaces.description: This agent, described for A2A clients.

surfaces.name: MCP server
surfaces.description: Streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint, no auth. audit_site(url) runs the fast agent-readiness audit, the same work as the audit-a-site skill; tools/list enumerates the rest. Discovery document at https://www.mattpyle.com/.well-known/mcp-server.

surfaces.name: MCP Server Card
surfaces.description: The MCP endpoint's identity, transport and protocol versions, per SEP-2127. Also served at https://www.mattpyle.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json.

surfaces.name: Agent Skills index
surfaces.description: Agent Skills Discovery index listing 2 skills with sha256 digests: https://www.mattpyle.com/.well-known/agent-skills/implement-markdown-negotiation/SKILL.md and https://www.mattpyle.com/.well-known/agent-skills/using-mattpyle-com/SKILL.md.

surfaces.name: ARD catalogue
surfaces.description: Agentic Resource Discovery publisher catalogue pointing at the A2A Agent Card, the MCP Server Card and the two Agent Skills.

surfaces.name: Poppy discovery document
surfaces.description: Personal Agent Protocol poppy.json, draft 0.2: protocol version, organization and an empty web object only, because the draft requires an OAuth issuer for every other member and this site has no sign-in.

surfaces.name: Steward's Signature Agent Card
surfaces.description: The Web Bot Auth identity of the steward-audit auditor and its OAuth Client ID Metadata Document. Signed Steward requests name it in Signature-Agent with type=cimd.

surfaces.name: Steward's key directory
surfaces.description: The Ed25519 public keys that verify Steward request signatures, as a JWK Set.

surfaces.name: scorecard.json
surfaces.description: Every scorecard run as JSON, the same numbers the scorecard page displays.

surfaces.name: activity.json
surfaces.description: Agent-traffic counts as JSON, at UTC-hour resolution.

writing.title: How to implement WebMCP on a website
writing.description: Add WebMCP to an existing website using Chrome's origin trial, document.modelContext, validated tool handlers, and six working examples.

writing.title: Hello, World! Or, this post is a lie.
writing.description: Testing Temporal workflows, deterministic standards, and agentic AI to build an editor for my website

writing.title: Accessibility, AI, and testing with screen readers
writing.description: AI built this site. Every automated tool gave it top marks. Then I installed a screen reader for the first time, spent an evening fumbling with it, and heard what my site actually sounds like.

projects.title: Argus
projects.description: A persona inspector. Each day it visits a site as one kind of visitor, such as a recruiter or a screen-reader user, and files what that visitor wanted and did not get. A finding waits for a verdict before anything is fixed.

projects.title: Steward
projects.description: An agent-readiness auditor and this site's editorial agent, built on Temporal. It checks what a site tells an agent over plain HTTP, then opens the pages in a real browser for Lighthouse and axe-core. Each run is a durable workflow that survives a worker restart.

projects.title: mattpyle.com
projects.description: This site. An Astro 7 personal site, mostly static, with server routes on Vercel for /mcp, /a2a and /activity, used as a live testbed for emerging web/agent standards — llms.txt, agents.md, Lighthouse's Agentic Browsing audits.

changelog.title: /activity shows who an agent is
changelog.summary: /activity now shows how many agent hits proved who sent them, names the key directories behind signatures the site does not yet recognise, and lists the MCP clients that give a name and a protocol revision.

changelog.title: Steward measures an agent's reading budget
changelog.summary: The agent audit and the nightly scorecard now measure how much of the first 8,000 characters an agent reads on each page is content rather than navigation, as text and as markdown, so a header that eats an agent's first read shows up as a number.

changelog.title: A guest book an agent can sign
changelog.summary: The retro homepage gets 1997 functionality: a guest book, a web ring, and a visit counter. The guest book is the first place on this site where an agent can create content, through WebMCP.

changelog.title: Added a /webmcp page to showcase WebMCP functionality
changelog.summary: The tools this site hands to agents get a page built from the live tool objects, with runnable examples.

changelog.title: Retro mode: a 1997 skin an agent can switch on
changelog.summary: A 1997 GeoCities-era appearance, and set_appearance: the site's first WebMCP tool that changes something instead of returning data, in your browser only.

changelog.title: The Scorecard gets a memory
changelog.summary: Redesigned /scorecard around a prominent latest run and a compact, expandable history, so score movement stays legible without creating a detail page for every audit.

changelog.title: Homepage activity now comes from the changelog
changelog.summary: The homepage's hand-maintained activity list is now a linked preview of the public changelog, with explicit dates and deterministic same-day ordering.

changelog.title: Public changelog launches
changelog.summary: A reverse-chronological log of what ships on this site — launches, features, infrastructure, and experiments. Starting with this page.

changelog.title: WebMCP read-only tool surface
changelog.summary: Registered three read-only, agent-callable WebMCP tools behind Chrome's origin trial — pure progressive enhancement, removable in one step, and consumed by approximately nothing.

changelog.title: Raw-markdown post variants + content negotiation
changelog.summary: Every post now has a token-efficient raw-markdown sibling at /writing/<slug>.md, and the canonical URL itself serves markdown when a request genuinely prefers it. Took three attempts to land the negotiation.
